1463:
The city manager shall pass upon each application and shall not approve the application of an applicant if in his opinion the applicant is not of good moral character or competent to safely operate a passenger motor vehicle for hire. If an applicant is rejected by the city manager, such applicant may, by a written request filed with the city manager within ten days after such rejection, appear personally before the mayor and council for a review of his application. The action of the mayor and council shall be final.
(Code 1967, § 28-1.2; Ord. No. 7-1972, § 3, 4-18-1972; Ord. No. 2013-126, § 2, 3-19-2013)
1464:
Before any application is finally passed upon by the city manager, the applicant shall exhibit a current motor vehicle operators license with all required endorsements issued by the state.
(Code 1967, § 28-1.3; Ord. No. 7-1972, § 4, 4-18-1972; Ord. No. 2013-126, § 3, 3-19-2013)
1465:
Upon approval of an application and payment of a permit fee of $5.00, the chief of police shall issue a permit to operate a passenger motor vehicle for hire in the city to the applicant which shall bear the name, address, age, signature and photograph of the applicant. Such permit shall be in effect for the remainder of the city's licensing year. A permit for each year thereafter shall be issued upon the payment of $2.00 unless the permit for the preceding year has been revoked, in which event a new application is required.
(Code 1967, § 28-1.4; Ord. No. 7-1972, § 5, 4-18-1972)
1466:
Each driver of a passenger motor vehicle for hire shall post his driver's permit in such vehicle as to be in full view of all passengers while such driver is operating said passenger motor vehicle for hire.
(Code 1967, § 28-1.5; Ord. No. 7-1972, § 6, 4-18-1972)
1467:
The mayor and council may at any time that it deems to the best interest and welfare of the city suspend or revoke any permit issued pursuant to this chapter. The mayor and council, if it desires to do so, may grant to such permit holder an opportunity to be heard before suspension or revocation is effected. The city manager may, upon recommendation of the chief of police, when he deems it to the best interest and welfare of the city, suspend any permit issued under the terms of this chapter, which suspension shall be effective until the next regular meeting of the mayor and council, at which time the mayor and council shall either reinstate, continue such suspension, or revoke such permit as it deems to the best interest and welfare of the city.
(Code 1967, § 28-1.6; Ord. No. 7-1972, § 7, 4-18-1972)
1468:
Before any vehicle for hire is licensed to be operated in the city, the owner or operator thereof shall exhibit a liability insurance policy written by a company with a Best's general policyholder rating of B or better on which the premium has been paid for at least one year which insures the occupants and the public against bodily injury and property damage in limits of not less than $25,000.00 for bodily injury or death of one person, $50,000.00 for bodily injuries or death of all persons injured or killed in any one accident, and property damage in any one accident in the amount of $25,000.00 and uninsured motorists coverage with the same minimum limits. Said policy shall provide that it shall not be cancelled or withdrawn until after 30 days notice in writing shall have first been given to the city, and said 30 days notice shall commence from the date notice is actually received at the offices of the city. In the event such policy is so cancelled or withdrawn, the license for the operation of the cab insured thereby shall be suspended until said policy is replaced with a like policy on which the premiums have been paid for at least one year.
(Code 1967, § 28-2; Ord. No. 1-1969, § 1, 1-7-1969; Ord. No. 2014-139, § 1, 1-7-2014)
1469:
The number of vehicles for hire licensed to operate in the city shall be limited to one for each 1,200 population according to the last census.
(Ord. of 3-20-1951, § 1; Code 1967, § 28-3; Ord. No. 2014-139, § 2, 1-7-2014)
1470:
All persons who operate passenger motor vehicles for hire in the city shall be governed by the following rules and regulations:
(1) Shall have a place of business to do business from and shall do business from said place of business and shall not park their vehicles not carrying passengers on the streets.
(2) Shall have their trade mark or name, telephone number and permit number shown on each side and rear of the cab or vehicle in permanent paint.
(3) Shall not cruise or park any vehicle or cab on any street in the city for the purpose of solicitation of business.
(4) Shall not have such office and place of business where beer is sold.
(5) Shall have all cabs and vehicles operated in said business inspected monthly for the purpose of safety to passengers, baggage and the public.
(6) Shall not operate any cab or vehicle or taxicab business just for a particular season or a special occasion.
(7) Shall not permit any cab or vehicle to be operated by a person under the influence of intoxicating liquors.
(Ord. of 11-21-1950, § 1; Code 1967, § 28-5)
1471:
(a) No interurban motorbus shall be parked or stopped upon any of the streets of the city within the present fire limits for the purpose of taking on or discharging any passenger, mail, packages, or luggage, and no passenger, mail, packages, or luggage shall be taken on or discharged from such bus while such bus is stopped on any street within the present fire limits of the city.
(b) As used in this section, interurban buses shall be construed to mean motorbuses transporting passengers for hire, and operated, from, into and between corporate cities or towns.
(Ord. of 12-1-1936, §§ 1, 2; Code 1967, § 28-11)

1474:
(a) The revision of the zoning ordinance of the city, copy of which is on file in the office of the city manager and made a part hereof, together with the official zoning map of the city, on file in the office of the city manager, all of which has been this day exhibited to and approved by the mayor and council of the city and has been placed on file in the office of the city manager, be and the same is hereby adopted and declared operative as provided therein, and binding within the then corporate limits of the city.
(b) The city clerk is hereby authorized, directed, and empowered, to insert at an appropriate place therein a certificate to the effect that said regulations constitute an official publication of regulations pertaining to zoning, and that said publication in book form, affecting said city, by authority and direction of the mayor and council of said city, is effective as the zoning ordinance of said city.
(Code 1967, § 29-1; Ord. No. 15-1972, 10-17-1972)
